## Device function tables for user functions (`get_device_func1`) {#sec-ch12-device-functions}

### Summary

A named user function, such as a saturation vapor pressure fit selected with `rate-constant: {formula: h2o_ideal}`,
is called through a table of function pointers. A CUDA kernel cannot call a host function pointer, so kintera keeps
two tables of the same functions: a host table for the CPU drivers and a device table for the CUDA kernels. Both are
indexed through one host list of names. The device table starts with a `nullptr` slot, so a name at position `id` of
the list is entry `id` of the host table and entry `id + 1` of the device table. Nothing checks that the two tables
hold the same functions in the same order: a function present in the host table but missing from the device table
gives wrong values on CUDA without an error (Limits). The steps to add a vapor-pressure law are in
@sec-ch02-svp, "Adding a vapor-pressure law"; this section explains the tables those steps edit.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Map a function name to a callable on the CPU and on CUDA, @eq-ch12-device-functions-index.

**Data.** Host name list `func1_names`; host table `func1_table_cpu`; device table `func1_table_cuda`.

**Placement.** Before each CPU loop or CUDA launch that evaluates named functions.

**Activation.** Every named `formula`[^rg-d2b95ba9579e] and its `_ddT` derivative; the empty name and `null` give no function.

**Guarantee / limits.** An unknown name raises an error; a host-device table mismatch is not detected.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Local symbols: $n$, a requested function name; $\mathrm{id}(n)$, its position in `func1_names`, counted from 0;
$h(n)$ and $d(n)$, the index used in the host and in the device table.

### Derivation

No derivation beyond the index rule. For a requested name $n$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
h(n) &= \mathrm{id}(n) , \\
d(n) &= \mathrm{id}(n) + 1 \quad \text{(registered name)}, \qquad d(n) = 0 \quad \text{(empty name or null)} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch12-device-functions-index}

Slot 0 of the device table is the `nullptr` placeholder, so $d(n) = 0$ gives a null pointer, which the kernels skip.
@eq-ch12-device-functions-index is computed in `get_host_func`
({{< code src/utils/user_funcs.hpp get_host_func >}}) for $h$ and in `get_device_func1`
({{< code src/utils/user_funcs.cu get_device_func1 >}}) for $d$.

### Numerical method

The lookup runs on the host before every evaluation:

1. **Names.** The caller passes the names of the functions to evaluate, for example the `formula` of each nucleation
   reaction and the same names with `_ddT` appended for their derivatives.
2. **CPU.** `call_func1_cpu` ({{< code src/utils/utils_dispatch.cpp call_func1_cpu >}}) and the saturation-adjustment
   CPU drivers call `get_host_func` with `func1_names` and `func1_table_cpu`. Each name is searched for in
   `func1_names` and replaced by the host pointer at the same position.
3. **CUDA.** `call_func1_cuda` ({{< code src/utils/utils_dispatch.cu call_func1_cuda >}}) and the saturation-adjustment
   CUDA drivers, for example `call_equilibrate_tp_cuda`
   ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_dispatch.cu call_equilibrate_tp_cuda >}}), call `get_device_func1` with the same
   `func1_names`. It builds the list of indices $d(n)$ on the host, copies it to the device, reads the address of the
   device table from the constant `func1_table_device_ptr`, and gathers the device pointers at those indices.
4. **Evaluation.** The CPU loop or the CUDA kernel calls each non-null pointer once per cell; a null pointer adds
   nothing.

"Function f not registered." is raised, on both devices, only when a name is not in `func1_names` and is neither
empty nor `null`. Because both lookups use the one host list, a name registered there is accepted on CUDA even if the
device table lacks it.

Registering a function therefore means editing three lists in the same order: the function and its derivative,
written as `DISPATCH_MACRO` functions in `src/vapors/vapor_functions.h` so that they compile for both devices, are
appended to `func1_table_cpu` ({{< code src/func_table.cpp func1_table_cpu >}}) and their names to `func1_names`
({{< code src/func_table.cpp func1_names >}}), and the same two functions to `func1_table_cuda`
({{< code src/func_table.cu func1_table_cuda >}}), after the `nullptr` placeholder and at the same positions. The
tables for functions of two and three arguments, `func2_table_cuda` and `func3_table_cuda`, follow the same
convention: the placeholder first, then the entries of `func2_table_cpu` and `func3_table_cpu` in the same order.
Both host tables are empty at the pin, so both device tables hold the placeholder alone; from
`e357792d50639d68e9090b542edf038d2b029aa2` on, `func2` carries the H2 rotational entries and its device table
carries the same names behind the placeholder. @fig-ch12-device-functions-tables shows the three lists.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_reaction_equilibrium.py` (`test_documented_native_curves`) | the 11 named curves, through the dispatch, equal their formulas, on CPU and on CUDA | $10^{-11}$ in $\ln K$ | not stated in the test |

: Tests of the device function tables. {#tbl-ch12-device-functions-tests}

The CUDA instance of `test_documented_native_curves` would catch a shifted device table for those 11 names: a shift
returns another curve's values. It passes on a CUDA build, and its CUDA instance skips on a CPU build.[^ch12-devfn-test]
No test evaluates the `_ddT` entries on CUDA.

The length-and-order property that no test covers is checked instead by `check_ch12_twins.py`, statically and with
no GPU: line a reads "func1: 22 names, 22 host, 23 device slots; host==names True, device==[nullptr]+names True
PASS", which is @eq-ch12-device-functions-index asserted over the whole table rather than over the 11 named curves,
and line b applies the same relation to the two- and three-argument tables, requiring each device table to be the
placeholder followed by its host table in order: it reads "func2/func3: host []/[], device
['nullptr']/['nullptr'] PASS" at the pin, where both host tables are empty, and keeps holding when a host table
is filled.[^ch12-kernels-check] A check that reads the source
cannot replace the runtime test: it would not catch a device table whose *entries* point at the wrong functions,
only one whose names or length disagree.

(1 passed, 1 skipped); CUDA 12.6.85, Python 3.11.13, torch 2.10.0+cu126, pytest 9.1.1.]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- **A function missing from the device table gives wrong values on CUDA, not an error.** Two cases were measured with
  a scratch build in which a test function returning $\ln K = 7$ (and its derivative) was added to `func1_table_cpu`
  and `func1_names` only. Appended at the end, it evaluated to 7 on the CPU and to 0 on CUDA: its device index
  $\mathrm{id}+1$ points past the end of the device table, and the slot read there was null, so the kernel added
  nothing. Inserted at the front, it shifted every later name by two device slots. On CUDA, `h2o_ideal` then returned
  the values of `h2o_bryan` ($\ln K$ = 4.559 against 4.333 at 250 K), the test function returned those of
  `h2o_ideal`, and the last registered name returned 0. In every case no error was raised.[^ch12-devfn-scratch]
  Reading past the end of a device array is undefined; that it reads a null pointer on other builds is a hypothesis.
:::

- The device table is a fixed array compiled into the CUDA library; adding a function needs a rebuild of both
  libraries.
